youtube.title: Someone Is at Your Door — whispered trip-hop jazz-funk: a round bass, a muted trumpet, a dusty kit
youtube.description:
Whispered jazz-funk / downtempo trip-hop in F minor at 70 BPM, swung: a round synth bass, a Harmon-muted trumpet and a dusty boom-bap kit under a man who notices ordinary things slightly out of place. Hypnotic, casually funny, a little suspicious. In the vein of late-night trip-hop and spoken-word jazz.
Spoken word, 5:08. Someone is at your door. He doesn't get up.

The bass plays one two-bar figure of four notes the whole way through; it never changes its notes, it only opens its filter and picks up grit. The kit is lazy and dry, with the ride on its own level. The muted trumpet is a second character: three wandering notes, a shrug, a silly falling "bah... ba-bwaaah", the motif a half-step higher. The narrator whispers four observations, the door, the lights, the curtain, the glass, in a turning order so no line comes back twice in a row; a line that returns is sometimes only half of itself, and sometimes a voice around him answers the half he left out. Those voices, far left, right, and distant, only ever repeat what he has said. Twice the band leans in and plays harder for four bars. In the climax the voices pile up around him, all of them land on the word "door", and the song stops dead.

Words: written for this song. Voices: synthetic whispered speech (Azure AI Speech), one clip per line, placed by hand on the beat; nobody's recorded voice is in it. Kit: a boom-bap kit and toms from GBS Jazz (Figure Drum Kits by tripjazz, Freesound, CC0). Trumpet: a General MIDI muted trumpet soundfont. Bass: Strudel's own synth.

Chapters
0:00 Intro — the bass and the kick, three wandering trumpet notes
0:11 Someone is at your door
0:52 The lights are on downstairs
1:34 The band plays harder
1:47 The curtain is open again — the glass on the table
2:28 Door, lights, curtain, glass
3:23 Harder again
3:37 Everybody's talking — then everyone on "door"
4:59 Outro — the door, again; the lights still on

Play and edit this song in your browser at jonborchardt.github.io/strudel-bench — press play, drag a slider, change a note, hear it immediately. Nothing to install. 

Every song here is a text file. This one is songs/someone-at-your-door.strudel in the repo, along with the harness that plays it:
https://github.com/jonborchardt/strudel-bench

strudel-bench is a live-coding harness where a song is a text file written in a high-level language: parts, sections, and twelve musical axes (density, brightness, weight, space, articulation and so on) that a phrase like "darker and more spacious" can move. Most of the code and the songs were written by coding agents working from a written spec, in the spirit of my blog, "always shippable, always improving":
https://jonborchardt.github.io/blog/

The video is not a screen recording. It is generated from the song itself: every hit in the music drives the animation, and the world it plays in is chosen from the song's own musical features.

Built on Strudel, the JavaScript port of TidalCycles: https://strudel.cc
Samples come from the public Strudel packs, each under its own license: https://strudel.cc/learn/samples/
